summary: Create one clearly named local service account (for example `ansible` or `aapsvc`) on each managed node so jobs keep running if external auth fails; give it enough privilege, SSH key auth only, and access only from controller and execution nodes. Use `become`/`become_user` to act as other users; create it with `useradd ansible --system --create-home`.
questions: What user should AAP use to connect to managed nodes?
Should the AAP service account be local or LDAP?
How do I create the ansible service account on RHEL?
Do I need to connect as a different user to run tasks as another user?

answer_card.title: Create the managed node service account
answer_card.answer_md:
```bash
sudo useradd ansible \
    --system --create-home \
    --comment "Ansible Automation Platform service account"
```
Keep it local, SSH-key only, and reachable only from controller and execution nodes. Use `become_user` for other users.
